problem_type: High-frequency canvas position updates cross the React Flow projection and subscription boundary
symptom: During real canvas dragging, React Flow edge-layer DOM mutations can scale with pointer moves because position changes are written to the domain store and fed back through a controlled nodes projection; related whole-graph selectors also invalidate readers that only need one node or a scalar.
direct_cause: GenerationCanvasReactFlow.handleNodesChange calls the domain moveNodes action for every position change while React Flow receives nodes={flowNodes}; every tick therefore replaces the store nodes array and re-runs the canvas projection and React Flow reconciliation. Several mounted readers additionally subscribe to state.nodes/state.edges or allocate derived arrays in selectors.
class_root: Transient interaction geometry, durable canvas state, graph edge projection, and per-node subscriptions do not have one enforced ownership boundary. A pointer sample must stay in the interaction kernel; durable store writes and graph projection updates must happen only at the shared commit boundary, while readers must subscribe to the smallest stable value they consume.
affected_population: Creators dragging one or more generation canvas nodes
Projects with dense graph edges or many mounted canvas cards
macOS Electron canvas sessions; Windows, clean install, and provider-backed generation remain unverified
entry_points: React Flow onNodesChange during a node drag
Per-node Zustand selectors for graph relationships and generation readiness
Canvas performance MutationObserver and React commit probes
external_sources: @xyflow/react controlled node store and edge renderer
internal_only_reason: The performance invariant is Nomi's canvas ownership contract; the existing Electron walks and production store are the authoritative user path.
invariants: A pointer-move position change does not write the durable canvas store or rebuild the graph projection.
Normal drag stop, cancel, blur, and lost-pointer paths have one shared writeback owner.
Position-only changes preserve edge structure and edge DOM identity.
A per-node reader never subscribes to the whole nodes/edges collection when a stable scalar or keyed projection is sufficient.
Performance evidence separates childList records, attribute records, React commits, long tasks, and actual component renders.

door_reduction.why_not: The framework boundary, drag draft, commit writeback, projection, relationship selectors, and stable off-canvas selector remain separate responsibilities; the fix makes their shared ownership explicit rather than hiding them behind one adapter.

generality_proof: Every canvas position gesture enters through React Flow onNodesChange and every mounted relationship reader consumes the same store collections. Fixing the kernel-to-store boundary and keyed selector boundary covers single-node, multi-node, dense-edge, and group-adjacent callers.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Keep drag samples in the React Flow kernel and route only authorized keyboard/commit changes to the store.
Update only React Flow's transient nodeLookup geometry without replacing the durable node projection.
Commit final dragged positions once and share normal/cancel/lost-pointer cleanup.
Keep position-agnostic readers reference-stable across position-only store churn.
Use WeakMap keyed relationship projections so each node reads a stable scalar instead of scanning or allocating from the whole graph on every notification.

recurrence.reason: The same leak can return through a new React Flow event handler, a new whole-graph selector, or a new derived array returned from a selector.

prevention.invariant: Pointer-move geometry stays in React Flow's kernel; durable writes and graph projection changes happen only at the shared commit boundary.
prevention.failure_mode: A future per-move store write or whole-graph selector causes edge-layer childList growth, commit amplification, or non-owner re-renders in the fixed benchmark.
prevention.exception_policy: Keyboard moves and explicit non-drag edits may commit through their existing authorized path.
prevention.strategy: Keep the existing kernel draft and projection sync helpers mounted, add mutation classification and selector regression tests, and gate the real Electron benchmark on edge childList and identity behavior.

legacy_paths.rationale: The existing kernel draft and projection sync helpers are restored as the shared path; no persisted data path is removed.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency is added or removed.

migration: No persisted schema migration. Existing node positions remain the durable source and are updated once at drag commit.
residual_risks: React Flow internals may change across @xyflow/react upgrades; rerun the kernel ownership contract and real DOM identity benchmark after upgrades.
The current local benchmark is macOS arm64; Windows and clean-install evidence remain unverified.
Real media proof uses repository 1920x1080 H.264 fixture and real imported fixture assets; provider-backed generation and user-specific projects remain outside this receipt.

invariant_owner_layer.why: All pointer-move position changes enter this React Flow boundary before either the kernel or durable store can receive them.
